newsitem.title: USA: Actor Charlton Heston seeks seat on NRA board.
newsitem.headline: Actor Charlton Heston seeks seat on NRA board.

text.p: A new, temporary sign, "Firearms are not permitted inside the Convention Centre," welcomed visitors to the Washington State Convention and Trade Centre Saturday, where the National Rifle Association is holding its annual meeting.
Convention delegates discussed actor Charlton Heston's announcement Friday that he would seek a seat on the NRA's board.
"Am I here to take over? No. Am I here to take sides? You better believe it," the 72-year-old actor told delegates.
Fliers in support of Heston's candidacy were passed around Saturday, showing him in a cowboy hat with a rifle over his shoulder.

Heston announced his candidacy and affirmed his support of the leadership of the national organisation of owners of firearms. He supports executive vice president and manager Wayne LaPierre, who has been under fire for the handling of the organisation's finances.
In a speech to members, LaPierre vigorously defended his leadership of the 3-million-member NRA.
"If the NRA is about bank accounts instead of gun rights," LaPierre shouted, "then get yourself another guy."
